title: Analysis of coffee bean extracts by use of ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled to quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry
author: O’Driscoll

steps.title: Extract coffee bean metabolites
steps.instruction: Freeze green and roasted coffee beans with liquid nitrogen, grind them in a mill, weigh 2 g of ground coffee and extract with 25 mL LC‑grade water pre‑heated to 92 °C; stir the suspension for 6 min at 70–80 °C, then immediately place on ice to cool rapidly; centrifuge the cooled extract at 21 481 × g for 2 min; filter the supernatant through a 0.2 µm PVDF membrane; aliquot the filtrate into 1.5 mL vials, seal, and store remaining extracts at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare two separate stock solutions (final volume 10 mL each) using methanol or water according to compound solubility; weigh 1–8 mg of each standard and dissolve in the appropriate solvent: methanol stock contains caffeine, 5‑caffeoylquinic acid, vitamin B3, caffeic acid, catechol, and 1,2,4‑benzenetriol; water stock contains trigonelline hydrochloride, quinic acid, ferulic acid, and pyrogallol.

steps.title: Set up LC system
steps.instruction: Install a Titan C18 analytical column (100 mm × 2.1 mm, 1.9 µm) preceded by a Titan C18 guard cartridge (5 mm × 2.1 mm, 1.9 µm) on the Waters Acquity UPLC; set column temperature to 35 °C; keep the autosampler at 4 °C; prepare mobile phase A (water + 0.1 % formic acid, ultra‑pure 18.2 MΩ Ω water) and mobile phase B (acetonitrile + 0.1 % formic acid, LC‑MS grade); program the gradient as described in Table 1 and Table 2; set flow rate to 0.3 mL min⁻¹, injection volume to 10 µL, and total run time to 12 min.

steps.title: Configure MS parameters
steps.instruction: On the Waters Acquity G2 Q‑TOF, select electrospray ionisation with msE centroid acquisition in both positive and negative modes; set m/z scan range to 50–2000 Da, analyser to resolution mode (FWHM), and scan speed to 1 scan every 0.7 s; define two collision‑energy functions: function 1 low energy (no CE) and function 2 high energy with a ramp from 20 to 75 eV; for negative mode set capillary voltage 3.00 kV, sampling cone 40 V, extraction cone 4.0 V, source temperature 120 °C, desolvation temperature 450 °C, desolvation gas flow 800 L h⁻¹, cone gas flow 50 L h⁻¹; for positive mode set capillary voltage 3.00 kV, sampling cone 30 V, extraction cone 2.0 V, source temperature 120 °C, desolvation temperature 450 °C, desolvation gas flow 800 L h⁻¹, cone gas flow 50 L h⁻¹.

steps.title: Calibrate mass accuracy
steps.instruction: Perform an initial mass calibration by direct infusion of a sodium iodide calibrant solution; then infuse leucine enkephalin lock‑mass solution (2 ng µL⁻¹) at 5 µL min⁻¹ parallel to the mobile‑phase flow, enable automatic lock‑mass correction to maintain mass accuracy < 5 ppm throughout the sequence.

steps.title: Run LC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Using MassLynx v4.1, load the prepared samples, start the LC‑MS run with the programmed gradient and MS settings, and acquire data for each injection; after the sequence, process the data in MassLynx as required.
